items.followUp: Define centrifugal force and write its formula.

rubric.why: This identifies the direction and role of centripetal force.
rubric.description: Defines centripetal force as the force directed towards the centre that keeps an object moving in a circular path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition including its centre-directed nature or its role in circular motion.

rubric.why: The formula expresses centripetal force in terms of mass, speed and radius (or angular speed).
rubric.description: Gives a correct formula for centripetal force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct formula.

modelAnswer: Centripetal force is the force directed towards the centre of a circular path that keeps an object moving in that path.
Its formula is F = mv²/r, where m is mass, v is speed and r is the radius of the circular path.

items.followUp: What condition must be true for a system to be isolated?

rubric.why: An isolated system is unaffected by an external force, or has zero net external force.
rubric.description: States that no external force acts on the system, or that the net external force is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either equivalent condition.

rubric.why: The absence of a net external force means the system's total momentum is conserved.
rubric.description: States the resulting conservation of total momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct statement of momentum conservation.

modelAnswer: An isolated system is one on which no external force acts; equivalently, the net external force on it is zero.
The total momentum of an isolated system remains constant.

items.followUp: Define one newton in terms of mass and acceleration.

rubric.why: The SI unit of force is the newton, symbol N.
rubric.description: Names the SI unit of force and/or gives its symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for newton or N.

rubric.why: This gives the defining relationship between force, mass and acceleration.
rubric.description: Defines one newton as the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition, including the mass and acceleration values.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of force is the newton (N).
One newton is the force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² in a mass of 1 kg.

items.followUp: Define unlike parallel forces and give one example.

rubric.why: Like parallel forces are parallel and act in the same direction.
rubric.description: Defines like parallel forces as parallel forces acting in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both that the forces are parallel and that they act in the same direction.

rubric.why: A suitable example must describe forces that are parallel and point in the same direction.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of like parallel forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an example such as two downward forces acting on a body.

modelAnswer: Like parallel forces are forces whose lines of action are parallel and which act in the same direction.
For example, two downward forces acting on a body are like parallel forces.

items.followUp: What are solar cells? State one use of a solar cell.

rubric.why: A solar panel is formed by combining multiple solar cells electrically.
rubric.description: Explains that a solar panel is made by connecting a number of solar cells, in series and/or parallel.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a panel consists of interconnected solar cells.

rubric.why: Solar panels convert solar energy into electrical energy, which can be used by electrical devices.
rubric.description: Gives a correct use of solar panels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they generate electricity from sunlight or giving a suitable application.

modelAnswer: A solar panel is formed by connecting many solar cells together, in series and/or parallel.
Solar panels convert sunlight into electrical energy and are used, for example, in satellites and calculators.

items.followUp: A force has perpendicular components of 6 N and 8 N. Find its magnitude and direction relative to the 6 N component.

rubric.why: The components are treated as mutually perpendicular components of the force.
rubric.description: Identifies the given components as perpendicular components, such as Fₓ and Fᵧ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the two perpendicular components.

rubric.why: The resultant magnitude follows from Pythagoras' theorem.
rubric.description: Writes the formula for the magnitude of the resultant force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct resultant formula.

rubric.why: Applying the formula to the supplied component values determines the force magnitude.
rubric.description: Substitutes the component values into the formula and evaluates the magnitude with units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and evaluation when component values are supplied.

rubric.why: The ratio of the perpendicular components determines the force's direction.
rubric.description: Gives the correct relation for the direction of the resultant force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct direction relation; accept a correct angle if component values are supplied.

modelAnswer: Let the perpendicular components of the force be Fₓ and Fᵧ, measured in newtons.
The magnitude of the resultant force is R = √(Fₓ² + Fᵧ²) N.
Substitute the given component values for Fₓ and Fᵧ, then evaluate R in newtons.
The direction relative to Fₓ is θ = tan⁻¹(Fᵧ/Fₓ).

items.followUp: A screw gauge has a pitch of 0.5 mm and 50 divisions on its circular scale. Find its least count.

accept: distance moved in one complete rotation
rubric.why: The least count is defined using the screw gauge's pitch and scale divisions.
rubric.description: Defines least count as the smallest measurement that can be read, or the distance moved by the spindle for one circular-scale division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: The least count is calculated by dividing pitch by the number of divisions on the circular scale; the usual value is 0.01 mm.
rubric.description: Gives the formula and/or the usual least-count value of a screw gauge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula or the standard value with a correct unit.

modelAnswer: The least count of a screw gauge is the smallest length it can measure; it equals the pitch divided by the number of divisions on the circular scale.
The usual least count of a screw gauge is 0.01 mm (0.001 cm).

items.followUp: Define derived units and give two examples.

rubric.why: Base units are independent units and are not defined in terms of other units.
rubric.description: Defines base units as independent units that are not derived from other units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Metre, kilogram, second and ampere are examples of SI base units.
rubric.description: Gives two valid examples of base units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct examples.

modelAnswer: Base units are independent units that are not derived from other units.
Two examples of SI base units are the metre (m) and the kilogram (kg).
